newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher, new premier to be named.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher, new premier to be named.

text.p: Stocks closed slightly higher on Monday in slow trading as the pending appointment of a new Prime Minister held investors on the sidelines, brokers said.
The release of February trade figures had little impact on the market, they said.
The composite index ended 3.11 points higher at 679.64.
Domestic media said President Kim Young-sam was expected to name a new Prime Minister late on Monday or early on Tuesday.
"Trade was slow because of the imminent cabinet reshuffle this week," said Lee Duck-jae of Dongwon Securities.
Kim has launched a sweeping reshuffle of his administration aimed at restoring his reputation, badly tarnished by a scandal involving loans to failed Hanbo Steel Co.
The trade ministry reported the nation's customs-cleared trade deficit widened to $2.1 billion in February from a $1.6 billion shortfall a year earlier.
The January deficit, which soared due to almost a month of strikes, was revised downward to $3.39 billion from $3.48 billion, the ministry said.
Volume was thin with 26.96 million shares changing hands, against 37.8 million on Friday.
The market was closed on Saturday for a national holiday.
Gainers outpaced losers 442 to 336 with 127 unchanged.

Brokers said trading in blue chips was sluggish. Interest was instead focused on individual shares with prospects of good earnings. Samsung Electronics, a leading blue chip, fell 400 won to 57,600, while Hanhwa rose 800 won to 11,800 on expectations of improving earnings.
KEPCO gained 400 won to 25,200, backed by foreign buying. Brokers said expectations that the ceiling for the foreign stock ownership limit would be expanded sometime this week boosted sentiment.
